claims.claim: For d=δ⁺(D)≥1, a directed cycle of length at least d+1 can be found in polynomial time; additionally, n<d+k is an immediate sound NO condition. Thus the target is completely solved for k=1.
claims.evidence: Let P=v₁…v_p be an inclusion-maximal simple directed path. Every out-neighbor of v_p lies among v₁,…,v_{p−1}. If v_i is the earliest such neighbor, the d distinct out-neighbors occupy at most the p−i positions v_i,…,v_{p−1}; hence d≤p−i. Therefore v_i→…→v_p→v_i is a directed cycle of length p−i+1≥d+1. Greedy path extension and extracting this cycle are polynomial-time operations. For k=1 this always supplies the requested cycle. Independently, every simple cycle has at most n vertices, so n<d+k is a sound NO condition.
claims.witness: The maximal-path terminal vertex and its earliest out-neighbor explicitly witness a cycle of length at least d+1.
claims.search_method: Independent symbolic reconstruction, followed by exhaustive enumeration of all loopless digraphs of orders 2–4 with positive minimum outdegree.

claims.claim: For any integer L≥2, existence of a directed cycle of length at least L is exactly equivalent to a short-leg two-way linkage, yielding an explicit O(n^L(n+m)) exact algorithm.
claims.evidence: For an ordered tuple of L distinct vertices v₁,…,v_L with arcs v_i→v_{i+1}, delete v₂,…,v_{L−1}. If v_L reaches v₁, choose a simple return path; its internal vertices avoid the tuple's internal vertices, so its union with the tuple path is a simple directed cycle on at least L vertices. Conversely, L consecutive vertices of any cycle of length at least L form such a tuple, and the complementary cycle segment is the required return path. Enumerating at most n^L tuples and performing one linear-time reachability test for each costs O(n^L(n+m)); when L>n the algorithm immediately returns NO.
claims.witness: Either an enumerated L-vertex directed path plus a simple return path, or L consecutive vertices and the complementary segment of an existing long cycle.
claims.search_method: Proved both witness-transfer directions independently and exhaustively compared the two predicates for every threshold on all loopless digraphs of orders 2–4.

claims.claim: There is a polynomially checkable upper-bound certificate: if X is an independent vertex set and every arc entering X from outside X has its tail in S⊆V(D)\X, then every directed cycle has length at most n−|X|+|S|.
claims.evidence: For each x∈C∩X, its predecessor on a directed cycle C lies outside X because X is independent, and therefore lies in S by hypothesis. Two different vertices of C∩X cannot have the same predecessor because a cycle vertex has one successor on C. This is an injection C∩X→C∩S, giving |C∩X|≤|C∩S|≤|S|. At most n−|X| vertices outside X can occur, so |C|≤n−|X|+|S|. Independence and the entering-arc condition can both be checked in polynomial time.
claims.witness: The injective map sending each cycle vertex in X to its predecessor in S certifies the bound.
claims.search_method: Independent predecessor-injection proof plus exhaustive checking of 131,755 admissible graph/X/S cases on all loopless digraphs of orders 2–4.

claims.claim: For every fixed k≥3 there are 2-strong NO-instances of arbitrarily large order with n≥d+k and circumference exactly d+k−1.
claims.evidence: Set r=k−1≥2 and take a complete bidirected bipartite digraph with independent parts R,A of sizes r and a≥k. Deleting any vertex leaves both parts nonempty, and every two remaining vertices are mutually reachable directly or through the opposite part, proving 2-strongness. The outdegrees are a on R and r on A, so d=r. Every directed cycle alternates between the parts and consequently has length at most 2r; using every vertex of R and any r vertices of A attains length 2r=d+k−1. Also n=r+a≥r+k=d+k, and increasing a gives arbitrarily large order.
claims.witness: For any a≥k, the alternating cycle through all r vertices of R and r selected vertices of A has the asserted maximum length.
claims.search_method: Derived degrees, connectivity, and the alternating-cycle upper bound symbolically; also checked representative parameters k=3,…,6 by exact computation.

claims.claim: For every fixed k≥4 there are 2-strong NO-instances with arbitrarily large minimum outdegree and with n≥d+k; indeed their circumference is exactly d+3.
claims.evidence: Let Q be a complete bidirected q-vertex core, q≥3, with gates x,y, and let A be independent. Add A→Q and {x,y}→A. After any one deletion, a gate and a nonempty strong core survive; these give mutual reachability among all remaining vertices, so the digraph is 2-strong. Vertices of Q\{x,y} have outdegree q−1, those of A have q, and the gates have q−1+|A|, hence d=q−1. Each A-vertex on a cycle needs a distinct predecessor from {x,y}, so at most two occur and the circumference is at most q+2=d+3. The cycle x→a₁→z₁→…→z_{q−2}→y→a₂→x attains q+2. Taking |A|≥k−1 gives n≥d+k, while k≥4 makes d+3<d+k. Letting q grow makes d arbitrarily large.
claims.witness: The displayed cycle using all q core vertices and two independent vertices realizes circumference d+3.
claims.search_method: Independently checked all arc classes, deletion cases, degrees, and the predecessor injection; representative k,q,a instances were also evaluated exactly.

claims.claim: For every fixed k≥4, there are 2-strong NO-instances with arbitrarily large minimum outdegree and order, with n≥d+k and circumference exactly d+k−1.
claims.evidence: Put s=k−2≥2. Let Q be a complete bidirected core of size q≥s+1, let S⊂Q have size s, and let A be independent of size a≥k−1. Add A→Q and S→A. At least one gate survives any single deletion; together with the surviving complete core and arcs A→Q, this proves 2-strongness. Vertices in Q\S have outdegree q−1, vertices in A have q, and gates have q−1+a, so d=q−1. The certificate with X=A bounds every cycle by q+s. A cycle s₁→a₁→s₂→a₂→…→s_s→a_s→t₁→…→t_{q−s}→s₁ uses q+s vertices, proving circumference q+s=d+k−1. Finally n=q+a≥q+k−1=d+k. Taking q arbitrarily large makes both order and minimum outdegree arbitrarily large.
claims.witness: The gate-interleaving cycle through all core vertices and s independent vertices attains the certificate's upper bound.
claims.search_method: Independent parametric proof of connectivity, degrees, upper bound, and attainment, supplemented by exact checks for representative k=4,…,6 instances.

claims.claim: The target has a polynomial-time solution on semicomplete digraphs: such an input is YES exactly when n≥d+k, and a Hamiltonian directed cycle can be constructed when YES.
claims.evidence: The target's 2-strong promise implies strongness. Given a cycle C in a strong semicomplete digraph, insert any outside z for which c_i→z→c_{i+1}. If no such insertion exists, semicompleteness implies that every outside vertex z is exclusively of one of two types: C→z for every c∈C, or z→C for every c∈C. Indeed, one arc c_i→z propagates around C and forbids every reverse arc; if none exists, z→C throughout. Strongness forces both types and an arc u→v from the first type to the second, obtained at the first type transition on a path toward C. Replacing c_i→c_{i+1} by c_i→u→v→c_{i+1} enlarges C. Repetition yields a Hamiltonian cycle in polynomial time. Thus a promised semicomplete input has a cycle of length at least d+k exactly when n≥d+k.
claims.witness: At every augmentation step, either one insertible vertex or a cross-type pair u→v enlarges the current directed cycle; termination produces a Hamiltonian cycle.
claims.search_method: Reconstructed the full augmentation argument and exhaustively ran it on all 59,808 semicomplete digraphs of orders 2–5, including all 52,528 strong cases.

target_evidence: The source asks for an f(k)n^{O(1)} algorithm on arbitrary 2-strong digraphs. The draft does not provide one and expressly labels itself partial. Claim 1 gives an exact algorithm whose exponent is L=d+k, not a function confined to the multiplicative parameter factor; Claim 0 settles only k=1; Claim 6 settles only semicomplete inputs; and the certificate and obstruction families do not constitute an FPT algorithm or hardness resolution. They are nevertheless correct, material structural and special-case progress, so VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS and an ACCURATE partial-resolution label are warranted.
checks_performed: Confirmed the exact source target is an FPT-in-k find-or-report algorithm for arbitrary 2-strong digraphs.
Independently reconstructed every proof, including all quantifiers, degree calculations, deletion cases, circumference bounds, witness cycles, and both directions of the linkage equivalence.

The checker exhaustively covered 4,164 loopless digraphs of orders 2–4, including 2,429 positive-minimum-outdegree maximal-path cases, 12,420 linkage-threshold cases, and 131,755 admissible upper-certificate cases.
The checker exactly verified 8 bipartite-family instances, 12 two-gate instances, and 12 general gate-family instances across representative parameter ranges.
The checker exhaustively ran the constructive Hamiltonicity procedure on all 59,808 semicomplete digraphs of orders 2–5 and succeeded on every one of the 52,528 strong cases.
Used no web or unauthorized evidence, and did not inspect any revision prompt, retrieval database, treatment receipt, other arm, prior-run material, or other solution.
